name: halopsa_navigate
description: Discover available HaloPSA tools by domain. Returns tool names and descriptions for the selected domain. All tools are callable at any time — this is a help/discovery aid, not a prerequisite.

domain.description:
The domain to explore:
- tickets: Ticket management - list, get, create, update tickets and manage support workflow
- clients: Client/company management - list and get client information and relationships
- assets: Asset management - list and get hardware/software assets, configurations
- agents: Agent management - list and get support staff and technician information
- invoices: Invoice management - list and get billing and invoice information
- lookups: Reference data - read the tenant's ticket statuses, priorities, ticket types and Category 1-4 values, so ids and category strings are resolved live instead of hardcoded
- users: Contact management - search, get, create (with duplicate-prevention by email) and update (partial, including activate/deactivate) contacts
- sites: Site management - list sites, optionally scoped to one client

name: halopsa_lookups_get
description: Read HaloPSA's reference tables — ticket statuses, priorities, ticket types and the four categorisation trees (Category 1-4) — so ids and category values come from the live tenant instead of being hardcoded. Returns every requested table in one call. Use it before halopsa_tickets_create or halopsa_tickets_update to resolve a name to the id or string those tools expect.

kinds.description: Which reference tables to read. Defaults to all four. Ask for only what you need — categories is by far the largest.

category_type_id.description: Restrict categories to one of Halo's four categorisation trees: 1 = Category 1, 2 = Category 2, 3 = Category 3, 4 = Category 4. Omit to read all four; every row carries its own type_id either way.

tickettype_id.description: Ask Halo to restrict statuses and categories to those valid for this ticket type, as returned by the ticket_types kind. Worth passing before creating or updating a ticket, since Halo rejects a status or category the ticket type does not allow -- but whether it actually narrows the list depends on how the tenant configured those restrictions.

include_inactive.description: Include inactive/hidden rows. Off by default, since an agent writing a ticket should only pick from what is currently selectable.

limit.description: Maximum rows per kind (default: 200). Narrow with category_type_id or tickettype_id rather than raising this.

full_response.description: Return rows exactly as HaloPSA sends them instead of the fields needed to identify a value. Off by default: reference rows run to ~26 properties each, mostly SLA timers and workflow switches, and projecting cuts a reply to roughly a third.

name: halopsa_users_search
description: Search contacts by name or email

name: halopsa_users_create
description: Create a contact; refuses and reports the existing record if the email is already in use

client_id.description: HaloPSA client (company) this contact belongs to. Required by HaloPSA's Contact entity.

site_id.description: HaloPSA site this contact belongs to; defaults to the client's main site when omitted

name: halopsa_users_update
description: Update only the fields provided; set inactive to deactivate or reactivate a contact

name: halopsa_tickets_add_attachment
description: Attach a file (e.g. a CSV or HTML report) to a ticket. content is base64, or plain text with content_encoding "text". Max 10 MB after decoding. With note, a note action is added too and the file is attached to it. Hidden from the end user unless hidden_from_user is false. Returns the attachment id (and action_id), not the content.

content.description: File content: base64 (default), or the text itself with content_encoding "text".

content_encoding.description: "base64" (default) or "text" (UTF-8 text such as CSV or HTML, sent as is).

content_type.description: MIME type, e.g. text/csv. Inferred from the file extension if omitted.

note.description: Optional note to add to the ticket with the file, e.g. what the file is.

hidden_from_user.description: Hide the file (and note) from the end user. Default true.
